Jai Kishan Rajak, PhD

Trondheim, NorwayPhD in Chemical Engineering · NTNU

Environmental and materials researcher

I grew up in an Indian industrial town shaped by mining and heavy industry. That background gives a personal context to my interest in environmental challenges and the materials we use to address them.

My journey has taken me from geological sciences at IISER Kolkata to a PhD in chemical engineering at NTNU, bringing together an understanding of natural systems and the design of functional materials.

I investigate how contaminants interact with porous silica, polymers, carbon-based materials and mineral surfaces. My work spans PFAS and water remediation, selective recovery of battery metals, reactive transport and CO₂ capture, using batch experiments, column studies and material characterization.

I am interested in connecting molecular-scale understanding with separation and remediation technologies that work in complex environmental conditions. Collaboration across disciplines and learning from both laboratory studies and field challenges continue to shape my approach.

Explore publicationsGet in touch

Research interests

Functional materials for environmental challenges, from molecular-scale interactions to treatment systems.

Silica- and carbon-based material nano-network with polymer integration. Porous structure design, and Interfacial engineering.

Water treatment & emerging contaminants

PFAS and other persistent contaminants, adsorption selectivity, natural-water chemistry, regeneration and reusable sorbents.

Carbon capture

Amine-functionalized porous silica, gas–solid adsorption, polymer loading and cyclic performance.

Separation technologies & resource recovery

Functional materials for selective separation, contaminant remediation and recovery of valuable resources, including battery-metal ions. Linking adsorption and continuous-flow treatment with emerging separation approaches.

Environmental geoscience & transport

Groundwater chemistry, contaminant–mineral interactions, reactive transport and continuous filtration in porous media.

Materials & methods

Functional materials

Mesoporous silica, aerogels, PEI/APTES, graphene, biochar, hydroxyapatite, clays and layered materials.

Characterization & analysis

BET/BJH, XRD, FTIR, Raman, TGA/DSC, STEM/TEM, AFM, DLS, zeta potential, LC-MS/MS, ICP-MS/OES, MP-AES and UV–Vis.

Experimental & computational methods

Batch and fixed-bed studies, kinetics, isotherms, regeneration, breakthrough, HYDRUS, PHREEQC, Python and MATLAB.
